# cache-eviction.md

When memory pressure rises, the cache evicts the least recently used entries. This frees capacity without restarting the service.

# cache-aside.md

In cache-aside, the application checks the cache first and loads the database on a miss before storing the value.

# encryption.md

Encryption transforms plaintext into ciphertext using keys so stored data is unreadable without decryption.

# backpressure.md

Backpressure slows producers when consumers fall behind, preventing queues from growing without bound.

# privacy-standard.md

Personal data controls require encryption while stored, log redaction, and periodic access reviews.

# write-ahead-log.md

The write ahead log records changes before data pages are modified so recovery can replay committed operations.

# write-through.md

In write-through caching, writes update the cache and persistent store together before returning success.

# rate-limit.md

A rate limiter throttles clients that exceed the allowed request budget and returns retry guidance.

# hashing.md

Hashing creates a one way digest for passwords and integrity checks; it is not reversible encryption.

# client-resilience.md

Clients retry temporary network failures with jittered exponential backoff until their retry budget is exhausted.

cases.query: How does the system make room when RAM is scarce?

candidate_sources.content:
# java-coffee.md

Java coffee is stocked in the break room and should be reordered when supplies are low.

# cache-eviction.md

When memory pressure rises, the cache evicts the least recently used entries. This frees capacity without restarting the service.

# polling.md

Polling repeatedly asks a service whether new data is available at fixed intervals.

# cache-aside.md

In cache-aside, the application checks the cache first and loads the database on a miss before storing the value.

# shard-rebalance.md

The cluster rebalances shards whenever a node joins, moving partitions until storage is evenly distributed.

cases.query: What protections apply to personal data?

candidate_sources.content:
# privacy-standard.md

Personal data controls require encryption while stored, log redaction, and periodic access reviews.

# encryption.md

Encryption transforms plaintext into ciphertext using keys so stored data is unreadable without decryption.

# write-ahead-log.md

The write ahead log records changes before data pages are modified so recovery can replay committed operations.

# schema-migration.md

Schema migrations add nullable columns first, migrate data, then enforce constraints in a later release.

# polling.md

Polling repeatedly asks a service whether new data is available at fixed intervals.

# authentication.md

Authentication verifies the identity of a user by checking credentials or signed tokens. Authorization is handled later.

# authorization.md

Authorization decides whether an authenticated user may perform an action on a protected resource. Authentication is assumed complete.

# provisioning.md

Provisioning creates accounts, permissions, and initial resources before a user starts.

# hashing.md

Hashing creates a one way digest for passwords and integrity checks; it is not reversible encryption.

# feature-flag.md

Feature flag checkout_v2_enabled controls access to the new checkout flow.

# audit-retention.md

Audit logs are retained for seven years and retention policies purge records only after the compliance window closes.

# observability.md

Observability combines logs, metrics, and traces to explain system behavior during incidents.

# backpressure.md

Backpressure slows producers when consumers fall behind, preventing queues from growing without bound.

# traces.md

Traces connect spans across services to show the path and timing of a single request.

# poison-pill.md

A poison pill message intentionally tells workers to stop processing and shut down cleanly.

# rate-limit.md

A rate limiter throttles clients that exceed the allowed request budget and returns retry guidance.

# canary.md

A canary release sends a small percentage of traffic to the new version before broad rollout.

# two-phase.md

Two phase commit asks participants to prepare and then commit only after every participant votes yes.

# cache-aside.md

In cache-aside, the application checks the cache first and loads the database on a miss before storing the value.

# lease.md

A lease grants temporary ownership and expires automatically if the holder stops renewing it.

cases.query: How should transient network failures be retried?

candidate_sources.content:
# client-resilience.md

Clients retry temporary network failures with jittered exponential backoff until their retry budget is exhausted.

# retry-policy.md

Transient network errors use exponential backoff with jitter and stop after the configured retry budget.
